analysis: Examined two changed files. (1) .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py: the only change is in LifecycleTests.setUp (head lines 927-931), which pins GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT="1" in the synthetic test environment so a CI re-run (attempt 2) does not trip the MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED path. This is test-only code in the threat-review tooling and does not touch provider runtime, coordinator contract, keys, attestation or cache storage. The existing test test_manual_github_rerun_hands_off_without_any_paid_work (line 953) still overrides it to "2", so rerun-disabled behavior remains covered. The rest of the displayed text is unchanged context. (2) .github/workflows/release-provider.yml: the patch adds DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod to the qualify-sdk job env (head lines ~239-242) and updates a comment at lines 181-182. This makes the test job compile/test with production identity defaults regardless of branch. It only affects the test job's build environment; it does not alter the build/sign/publish jobs, which still take the environment from resolve-env.outputs.environment. No new permissions, secrets, or action pins; permissions stay contents: read. The change tightens test fidelity (tests see prod defaults on dev branch) and relates to the retained build qualification and artifact contract (A-017, T-054) only indirectly. No regression identified. Remaining integration question, outside supplied evidence: the workflow's full job graph and Package.swift environment handling were not visible, so I could not confirm that qualify-sdk output is not reused as a release artifact built with a different identity than the signed build job. Nothing visible suggests that.
